text: Explain the concept of Production Possibility Curve with an example and the diagram.
Explain Consumer Surplus and Producer Surplus.
Explain Consumer Equilibrium using Ordinal Utility Analysis.
Explain Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility.
Explain the effect of the following on the demand for a good: (i) Rise in income of its buyers (ii) Fall in income of its buyers.

A consumer wants to consume two goods: A and B. Good A is priced at Rs. 2 per unit and Good B at Rs. 4 per unit. The income of the consumer is fixed at Rs. 20. On the basis of this information, answer the following questions: (i) Mention the bundles which can be represented on the 'Budget Line'. (ii) How much units of good A can be purchased if the entire income is spent on that good? (iii) Write down the algebraic expression of budget line. (iv) Determine the slope of the budget line.

A company is selling wireless headphones and wants to fix a price so that exactly 60 units are sold. There are three major retailers in the market, and their individual demand functions are as follows: D1 = 50 - P, D2 = 40 - 0.5P, D3 = 30 - 0.5P. (i) Derive the market demand equation. (ii) Find the price per unit at which the company can sell all 60 units. (iii) Calculate how many headphones each retailer will purchase at that price.

If Elasticity of Demand = (-) 0.4 and change in quantity demanded = (-) 0.5, find new expenditure on the commodity if initial expenditure is Rs. 1500. Also comment upon the elasticity using Total Expenditure Method.

Suppose that an ice-cream is sold for Rs. 30. Ms. Ishani, who loves ice cream, has already eaten 3. Her marginal utility from eating 3rd ice-cream is 90 utils. If MU of Rs. 1 is 3 utils, should she eat more ice-creams or should she stop?
